issues.what: The planned tea-and-father's-last-river reveal (ch2) is replayed as new in ch12 (same 'knew the hand' line, now 'Joram Marrow') and again in ch14 from Quell's robe
issues.quote: This is the page, where Joram Marrow drew his last river.

issues.what: Master Hobb (bearded supervisor since ch1) is re-described as a twenty-year-old and called 'boy' in ch11
issues.quote: He was twenty, pimply, kind to stray cats in the map office yard.

issues.what: Ilse steps onto the landing and ties up to its ring, then draws a bridge to reach it and crosses; ch10 then draws a second footbridge as if the first never existed
issues.quote: She stepped onto the stone. It held firm under her boots

issues.what: Timeline: father dead six years (ch1) but sheet entered 'twelve years past, at trial'; ch14/15 say eleven; the folio 'came three days past' though it was yesterday; 'last week' in ch13
issues.quote: Sheet entered by the Surveyor General twelve years past, at trial of Joss Marrow

issues.what: Brief text pasted into dialogue/thought (ch13, ch14, ch15), and ch15 recaps the first night wrongly (atlas behind the turnip barrel, lock canal)
issues.quote: You inked a single footbridge into your book and woke to find it standing over the canal.

issues.what: Ilse's footbridge sketch is in Quell's portfolio in ch12 but in her own folio in ch13; ch13 retells how it was drawn (towpath, Tib counting) against ch10 (cabin roof)
issues.quote: She had drawn that bridge on the towpath to escape the crumbling shore.

issues.what: The grey skiff Ilse drew in ch2 vanishes; the crash is Dray's boat on a channel sketched 'at Pell's table' though ch1 has her in bed; 'Morning'/'this dawn' in the afternoon
issues.quote: She had been half asleep last night at Pell's table, folio open under a flour sack

issues.what: The folio is suddenly 'sewn inside the lining' and unpicked stitch by stitch in ch13, though she carries it buttoned in her coat
issues.quote: The hidden folio sewn inside the lining pressed against her ribs

issues.what: The erasure 'in my sleep' has no night to happen in; the whole story since ch1 is one day and night
issues.quote: I think I did it in my sleep

issues.what: Duplicate titles (ch10/11 'The Sealed Sheet'), near-duplicates (Brass Pens/Brass Divider, Early Bell/Tide Bell, Indigo Lamp/Blue Lamp), ch15 'Twelve Drowned Houses' is untrue
Repeated images: folio warm 'like bread fresh from the oven' in four chapters; 'soup' for mud, ink, water in eight
issues.quote: a faint warmth underneath like bread fresh from the oven

issues.what: Ilse recalls standing on Sunniva's deck 'that morning'; she never has
issues.quote: She tried to remember Sunniva's deck under her boots that morning

fix: Edits across all 15 chapters (no rewrites): align timeline (six years since hanging, twelve since fever year, one day since the folio); restore Hobb as the bearded master; ch8 keeps Ilse on the towpath until the bridge; ch10 has the first bridge collapse before the second; ch12 shows a different page (the fever cut kept back from court) and ch14 its hidden back; move the bridge sketch to Ilse's folio and match ch10; strip brief text from ch13-15; fix the skiff, sewn-folio, erasure-timing and Joram/Joss slips; retitle 11 chapters.
praise: Ilse's wry voice under pressure and the house-by-house redraw ending with the Silt Mother drawn 'with, not on top' are genuinely good.
